oracle.scope: Real CLI, structured and registry consumers expose separate process CPU and monotonic wall intervals. Explicit arithmetic fixtures check their distinct cumulative totals and omit gaps between invocation windows. Native sources are read without an external monitor. R keeps unavailable, regressing or source-changing intermediate counters unknown through completion and preserves unrelated measurements. Pure SRX generators themselves never read clocks. 6.d.C centralizes operational metric projection and the CLI summary adapter only; the same unchanged W/R behavior cases bind measurements, semantic parity, unknown handling and native authority boundaries.

preconditions: Current trusted runtime and real CLI/request/registry consumers; explicit process-local ledgers and clearly named counter fixtures for exact arithmetic.
R: trusted synchronous operational drivers; complete explicit SRX inputs and owned temporary payload/transaction roots; fixture-labelled samples only for exact arithmetic/failure injection.
steps: Run real environment commands with and without --metrics, including explicit selected-project error outcomes.
Reuse one owned ledger across completed windows and compare independent CPU/wall sums, RSS peaks and registered byte peaks.
Check machine values, measurement sources, unchanged semantic payloads and project inventories.
Drive real SRX/graph and bounded native payload work through pure interval signals; compare complete results and byte hashes with the unobserved execution.
Check intermediate unknown/regression/source changes, actual native publication phase boundaries and unchanged authority/receipt contracts for the selected cases.
